Name: Docker / OCI
Use Case: Local dev, CI build, base for all container orchestration
Strengths: Ubiquitous, huge image ecosystem (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR), reproducible builds
Notes: Use BuildKit + multi-stage builds + 'distroless' or 'chainguard' base images for tiny, vuln-free images.

Name: Podman
Strengths: Daemonless (no root), drop-in 'docker' CLI, pods (groups of containers)
Weaknesses: Smaller community, some Docker-only features behind
Notes: Great default on RHEL/Fedora; integrates with 'systemd' via 'quadlet'.

Name: containerd / CRI-O
Strengths: Lightweight, CRI-compliant, used by every major K8s distro
Weaknesses: Not a user-facing CLI by default
Notes: K8s 1.24+ removed dockershim; clusters now use containerd or CRI-O directly.

Name: Kubernetes
Use Case: Stateful & stateless workloads, batch (Jobs/CronJobs), service mesh substrate
Strengths: Industry standard, huge ecosystem, declarative, CRD-extensible
Weaknesses: Steep learning curve, operational cost; over-engineered for tiny apps
Keywords: kubernetes k8s pod deployment statefulset operator
Notes: Pin to N-2 minor versions; never run kube-proxy + Cilium without thinking through CNI choice.

Name: EKS / GKE / AKS
Use Case: Production K8s without managing the control plane
Notes: Karpenter (or cluster-autoscaler) + Bottlerocket for cheapest, fastest scaling on EKS.

Name: Helm
Notes: Use 'helmfile' or ArgoCD 'ApplicationSet' to orchestrate multi-chart deployments.

Name: Kustomize
Strengths: No templating, declarative, native to kubectl
Weaknesses: Limited logic; large overlays get unwieldy
Notes: Pair with ArgoCD; keep base = strict source-of-truth, overlays only for diffs.

Name: ArgoCD / Flux
Use Case: Continuous delivery for K8s from a Git repo
Strengths: Declarative deploys, drift detection, auto-sync, multi-cluster (ApplicationSet)
Weaknesses: Cluster bootstrap is its own problem (chicken-and-egg)
Notes: Use App-of-Apps / ApplicationSet patterns; keep secrets out of Git via External Secrets / Sealed Secrets.

Name: Istio / Linkerd / Cilium Mesh
Use Case: mTLS, traffic shifting, retries, observability between services
Strengths: Cross-cutting concerns out of app code
Keywords: istio linkerd cilium service mesh mtls
Notes: Linkerd is simplest; Cilium Mesh / ambient mode (Istio) reduce sidecar overhead via eBPF.

Name: Envoy
Use Case: Edge/internal proxy, mesh data plane, gateway
Strengths: High-performance C++, rich filter chain, gRPC-native
Weaknesses: Configuration complexity (xDS); usually managed by control plane (Istio, Gloo, Contour)
Notes: Underpins most modern meshes; 'Envoy Gateway' is the official K8s Gateway API impl.

Name: Ingress NGINX / Traefik / Envoy Gateway / Contour
Strengths: Mature, ubiquitous (NGINX); modern Gateway API impls (Contour, Envoy Gateway)
Weaknesses: Plain Ingress is limited; teams should adopt Gateway API
Notes: Migrate to Gateway API for advanced routing, traffic split, & multi-team ownership.

Name: Karpenter
Use Case: Just-in-time node provisioning on AWS / Azure
Strengths: Bin-packs better than cluster-autoscaler, picks cheapest instance type, fast scale-out
Notes: Set 'consolidation' to drop under-utilised nodes automatically; use 'spot' nodepools where workloads tolerate.

Name: HashiCorp Nomad
Use Case: Run containers, VMs, batch jobs with simpler ops than K8s
Strengths: Single binary, mixed workload types, no etcd
Weaknesses: Smaller ecosystem than K8s, fewer integrations
Notes: Sweet spot when you don't need K8s' API surface but want a real scheduler.

Name: Docker Compose
Notes: Use 'compose.yaml' (v3 spec); pair with Testcontainers for tests.

Name: Testcontainers
Use Case: Spin up real Postgres/Kafka/etc. per test
Strengths: High-fidelity integration tests, supports many languages
Weaknesses: Adds CI time; needs Docker in CI runner
Notes: Cache base images in CI; reuse via 'TESTCONTAINERS_REUSE_ENABLE=true'.
